questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the set of correct statements:
(A) Chrome steel is used for cutting tools and crushing machines.
(B) The fine dust of aluminium is used in paints and lacquers.
(C) Copper is used for reduction of alcohol.
(D) Zinc dust is used as a reducing agent in the manufacture of paints.
(E) Iron is used for galvanising zinc.
Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
Chrome steel is used for cutting tools and crushing machines while fine dust of aluminium is used in paints and lacquers.
Zinc dust is a reducing agent for manufacture of dye-stuffs and paints.
So, statements A, B and D are correct.
Copper is used for oxidation of primary and secondary alcohols into aldehydes and ketones respectively at high temperature. So, statement (C) is incorrect.
For galvanisation of iron, zinc is used to prevent iron from corrosion so, statement $(E)$ is also incorrect.
Hence, correct statements are (A), (B) and (D) only.

(b) Metal nitrates are highly soluble in water.
options: a is false but b is true

questions.q: The following reactions take place in the blast furnace in the preparation of impure iron. Identify the reaction pertaining to the formation of the slag.
questions.solution:
A slag is an easily fusible material which is formed when gangue still present in the roasted or the calcined ore combines with the flux. For example, in the metallurgy of iron, $\mathrm{CaO}$ (flux) combines with silica gangue to form easily fusible calcium silicate $\left(\mathrm{CaSiO}_3\right)$ slag.

\mathrm{CaO}+\mathrm{SiO}_2 \longrightarrow \mathrm{CaSiO}_3 \text { (slag) }

questions.solution:
Argentitie or Silver glance, $\mathrm{Ag}_2 \mathrm{~S}$ is an ore of silver. Silver is extracted from argentite by the mac-Arthur and Forest process (leaching process).
$\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{Ag}_2 \mathrm{~S}+4 \mathrm{NaCN} \rightarrow 2 \mathrm{Na}\left[\mathrm{Ag}(\mathrm{CN})_2\right]+\mathrm{Na}_2 \mathrm{~S} \\
& 4 \mathrm{Au}+8 \mathrm{KCN}+2 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}+\mathrm{O}_2 \rightarrow 4 \mathrm{~K}\left[\mathrm{Au}(\mathrm{CN})_2\right]+4 \mathrm{KOH}
\end{aligned}$
Related Theory
Leaching is the selective dissolution of the desired mineral leaving behind the impurities in a suitable dissolving agent.

questions.q: Which of the following statement, about the advantage of roasting of sulphide ore before reduction is not true?
options: The $\Delta \mathrm{G}_f^{\text {o }}$ of the sulphide is greater than those for $\mathrm{CS}_2$ and $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{~S}$.
The $\Delta \mathrm{G}_f^0$ is negative for roasting of sulphide ore to oxide
Roasting of the sulphide to the oxide is thermodynamically feasible
Carbon and hydrogen are suitable reducing agents for metal sulphides
questions.solution: The sulphide ore is roasted to oxide before reduction because the $\Delta \mathrm{G}$ of most of the sulphides are greater than those of $\mathrm{CS}_2$ and $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{~S}$, therefore neither $\mathrm{C}$ nor $\mathrm{H}$ can reduce metal sulphide to metal. Further, the standard free energies of formation of oxide are much less than those of $\mathrm{SO}_2$. Hence oxidation of metal sulphides to metal oxide is thermodynamically favourable.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: General Principles and Processes of Isolation of Metals
questions.q: The method of zone refining of metals is based on the principle of:
options: greater mobility of the pure metal that than that of the impurity
higher melting point of the impurity than that of the pure metal
greater noble character of the solid metal than that of the impurity
greater solubility of the impurity in the molten state than in the solid
questions.solution: The principle of zone refining is that the impurities in ore of metal are more soluble in the melted state when compared to the corresponding solid state of the impurities. In the zone refining process, the impurities are concentrated at one end of the block of metal so that the rest of the block is purified. Related Theory Zone refining process is very effective in the removal of impurities from semiconducting elements such as Germanium, Gallium, and Silicon. This process is also used in refining high-purity metals.

questions.solution:
In the extraction of copper from its sulphide ore, the metal is formed by the reduction of $\mathrm{Cu}_2 \mathrm{O}$ with $\mathrm{Cu}_2 \mathrm{~S}$. This reaction completes with the process of auto-reduction. Chemical reaction occuring in this reaction is as follows

The molten copper is allowed to cool. During cooling, dissolved $\mathrm{SO}_2$ comes out in the form of blisters, soit is called blister copper.
